lines.text: - **"choirmaster" (H5329 "to conduct", M76):** 10 psalm superscriptions (Psa 9:1, 11:1, 14:1, 36:1, 42:1, 45:1, 53:1, 57:1, 62:1, 69:1). The M47 word belongs to the psalm body. The heading has no bearing on it.

- **Quantity words in M46:** "abundance / greatness / multitude" of iniquity or idols (Jer 13:22; Hos 9:7; Eze 14:4), "numerous" (Deu 10:22), "to no avail" (Dan 11:27), "good for nothing" (Jer 13:10), "retinue" (1Ki 10:2). None of these is about wealth.
- "pity" (Psa 69:20) — *nûd*, a sympathetic shaking of the head
- "intoxicated" (Pro 5:20) — *šāgâ*, see §4.2
- "appointed" (Jon 4:8) and "count on" (2Co 10:2)
- **"heart" = "midst":** "the heart of the seas" (Eze 27:27).
- **"spokes" (Eze 10:12)** is tagged hand.
- "**The king's heart is a stream of water in the hand of the Lord; he turns it wherever he will**" (Pro 21:1)
- "the Lord … **had turned the heart of the king of Assyria** to them" (Ezr 6:22)
- "who **put such a thing as this into the heart of the king**" (Ezr 7:27)
- "God has **put it into their hearts** … handing over their royal power to the beast" (Rev 17:17)
- "his wisdom, which **God had put into his mind**" (2Ch 9:23)
- **Stirred:** Cyrus, Pul, the kings of the Medes (1Ch 5:26; 2Ch 36:22; Ezr 1:1; Jer 51:11) → Batch G §11.
- "the Lord **hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt**" (Exo 14:8; 4:21)
- "the Lord your God **hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate**, that he might give him into your hand" (Deu 2:30) [H1] (Sihon)
- "who **cuts off the spirit of princes**" (Psa 76:12) [H1]
- "He **takes away understanding** [*heart*] **from the chiefs** … and makes them wander" (Job 12:24)
- "the heart of kings is **unsearchable**" (Pro 25:3)
- "the mind of the king of Syria was greatly troubled" — Elisha tells "the words that you speak in your bedroom" (2Ki 6:11–12; see Batch A and Batch E)

**[Claude reading]** In the text the king's heart is the heart with the most power over others. It is also the heart shown **most often as acted upon**: God turns it, puts things into it, stirs it, hardens it, and cuts it off. The unsearchable heart of Pro 25:3 is unsearchable **to subjects**. To God it is a stream in his hand.
- "You said **in your heart**, 'I will ascend to heaven … **I will set my throne on high**'" (Isa 14:13)
- "**in his own mind he shall become great** … he shall even rise up against the Prince of princes" (Dan 8:25)
- "**in her heart she says, 'I sit as a queen**, I am no widow'" (Rev 18:7)
- "the **arrogant heart of the king of Assyria**" (Isa 10:12); "Your heart was proud because of your beauty … I exposed you **before kings**" (Eze 28:17)

- "when **his heart was lifted up and his spirit was hardened** … he was brought down from his **kingly throne**" (Dan 5:20). Then "**his mind was made like that of a beast** … **until he knew that the Most High God rules** the kingdom of mankind" (5:21). See Batch G §14.10.
- **The remedy in the law of the king:** he is to write out the law and "read in it all the days of his life … **that his heart may not be lifted up above his brothers**" (Deu 17:19–20).

- **The subject's version:** "Haman said **to himself** [*in his heart*], 'Whom would the king delight to honor more than me?'" (Est 6:6). Context 6:7–12: he describes the honour, **is made to give it to Mordecai**, and "hurried to his house, mourning and with his head covered" (6:12).

[Claude reading] Isa 14, Dan 8 and Rev 18 all use the same form: **the heart speaks a claim to rule**, and the fall follows. Deu 17 gives the only preventive, and it is a daily one: reading, so that the heart is not raised. Haman's inner sentence is the courtier's form of the same claim, and the reversal follows within the same scene.
| The king's longing | "the spirit of the king **longed to go out to Absalom**, because he was comforted about Amnon" (13:39). [verify] ESV supplies "spirit"; the verse is not in M47. |
| The heart read by another | "Joab … **knew that the king's heart went out to Absalom**" (14:1) → Joab stages the Tekoite woman's case |
| The heart held back | "he is **not to come into my presence**" (14:24) → after two years, "the king **kissed** Absalom" (14:33) |

| Hearts stolen | Absalom at the gate: "your claims are good and right, but **there is no man designated by the king to hear you**" (15:3). "he would … take hold of him and **kiss** him" (15:5). "**So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel**" (15:6). |
| The report | "**The hearts of the men of Israel have gone after Absalom**" (15:13) |
| Grief after victory | "O my son Absalom" (19:4). Joab: "your servants, who have this day **saved your life** … you love those who hate you" (19:5–6) |
| Hearts swayed back | "**You are my bone and my flesh**. Why then should you be the last to bring back the king?" (19:12–13) → "**he swayed the heart of all the men of Judah as one man**" (19:14) |

1. **Allegiance is a heart-matter, and it moves by attention.** Absalom wins hearts by standing where the king is absent (15:2–4) and by the kiss the king himself gave him (14:33 → 15:5). The heart follows whoever **hears the cause**.

2. **The king's own heart drives the plot.** The heart that "went out to Absalom" (14:1) opens the way for the son who steals every other heart. After the victory the same heart grieves, and nearly loses the army (19:6–7).

- **The same claim in the opposite direction:** Abimelech — "Remember also that **I am your bone and your flesh**" (Judg 9:2) → "**their hearts inclined to follow Abimelech**, for they said, 'He is our brother'" (9:3) → he kills his seventy brothers "on one stone" (9:5).
- "with **a whole heart to make David king** … of **a single mind** to make David king" (1Ch 12:38)
- "The hand of God was also on Judah to give them **one heart** to do what the king … commanded" (2Ch 30:12)
- Before: "you shall **reign over all that your soul desires**" (1Ki 11:37), on the condition of 11:38, "if you will … walk in my ways".
- "Jeroboam **said in his heart**, 'Now the kingdom will turn back …' **the heart of this people will turn again** to their lord … and they will kill me" (12:26–27).
- After: "So the king took counsel and **made two calves of gold**" (12:28).
- **Esther — the soul reversed.** Context read: Est 4:12–16; 5:6–14; 7:3–8.
- Mordecai: "**Do not think to yourself** [*in your nephesh*] that in the king's palace you will escape" (4:13) → "if I perish, I perish" (4:16).
- Then, at the wine: "**let my life be granted me** for my wish, and my people for my request" (7:3).
- The king "arose in his wrath from the wine-drinking … **Haman stayed to beg for his life** from Queen Esther" (7:7).
- **Ben-hadad and the prophet's parable.** Context read: 1Ki 20:31–43.
- **The king's anger costs a life:** "whoever provokes him to anger **forfeits his life**" (Pro 20:2). "let my life be **precious in your sight**" (2Ki 1:13–14; see Batch C).
- **The formula "into the hand of those who seek their life"** (Jer 19:7; 21:7; 22:25; 34:20–21; 38:16; 44:30; 46:26) → Batch G §5.3.

- ◆ **A reward for murder refused:** the murderers of Ish-bosheth: "your enemy, **who sought your life**. The Lord has avenged my lord the king" (2Sa 4:8) → David: "As the Lord lives, **who has redeemed my life** out of every adversity" → he has them killed (4:9–12). **The claim of vengeance on David's behalf is answered by an oath on David's own redeemed soul.**
- "**he who rules his spirit** [is better] than he who takes a city" (Pro 16:32) [H1]
- "If **the anger** [*spirit*] **of the ruler** rises against you, do not leave your place, for calmness will lay great offenses to rest" (Ecc 10:4) → Batch F §9.5 ("holding the spirit back")
- "let **the peace of Christ rule** [*umpire*] **in your hearts**" (Col 3:15)
- "having **his desire under control** [*authority over his own will*] … determined this **in his heart**" (1Co 7:37)
- "after it was sold, was it not **at your disposal** [*authority*]? Why is it that **you have contrived this deed in your heart**?" (Act 5:4)
- "while **applying my heart** … when **man had power over man** to his hurt" (Ecc 8:9); God "does not give him **power to enjoy** them" (Ecc 6:2)
- "**Let every soul be subject** to the governing authorities" (Rom 13:1)
- "**He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him**" (Mar 1:27; Luk 4:36). Authority over unclean spirits is **given** to the twelve (Mat 10:1; Mar 6:7) [O].

- **The formula without the authority.** Context read: Act 19:13–16. "I adjure you by the Jesus whom Paul proclaims" → "Jesus I know … **but who are you?**" → the man with the evil spirit "**mastered all of them**" (19:16) [O]. **The spirit masters those who use the name without the relation.**
- **Authority to give the Spirit, offered for money.** Context read: Act 8:13–24.
- **A spirit as someone's income:** "a slave girl who had **a spirit of divination** and brought **her owners** much gain" (Act 16:16) [O]
- "the **prince of the power of the air**, **the spirit that is now at work** in the sons of disobedience" (Eph 2:2) [O]
- "unless one is born of water and **the Spirit**, he cannot **enter the kingdom**" (Joh 3:5) [D3]; "**Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom**" (Mat 5:3) [H1]
- "if it is **by the Spirit of God** that I cast out demons, then **the kingdom of God has come** upon you" (Mat 12:28)
- "**the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking** but of … joy in the Holy Spirit" (Rom 14:17) → §7.6
- "**flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom**" (1Co 15:50)
- "strengthening **the souls** of the disciples … through many tribulations we must enter **the kingdom**" (Act 14:22)
- "hears **the word of the kingdom** … the evil one **snatches away what has been sown in his heart**" (Mat 13:19)

- Context 1Sa 26:21–27:4. **Saul's oath comes first:** "I will no more do you harm, because **my life was precious in your eyes** this day. **Behold, I have acted foolishly, and have made a great mistake**" (26:21). David: "as your life was precious this day in my sight, **so may my life be precious in the sight of the Lord**" (26:24). Saul: "Blessed be you, my son David!" (26:25).
- **Immediately after:** "Then **David said in his heart**, 'Now I shall perish one day by the hand of Saul'" (27:1) → he goes back to Achish (27:2) → "he no longer sought him" (27:4).

- [Claude reading] David does not answer Saul's promise with trust. He answers it by putting his life in the Lord's sight (26:24) and then **with a private sentence in his heart** that the promise will fail. The heart's reading of the king proves right: Saul stops only when David is out of reach. This adds context to the "said in heart" series (depiction v1 §2.1c; Batch B §0).
- "Go, **do all that is in your heart**, for the Lord is with you" (7:3)
- "But **that same night** the word of the Lord came to Nathan" (7:4)
- David's own later account: "**I had it in my heart** to build … But God said to me, 'You may not'" (1Ch 28:2–3)
- **The heart that despised the king.** "Michal … saw King David leaping and dancing … and **she despised him in her heart**" (2Sa 6:16; 1Ch 15:29).
- After: it becomes speech — "How the king of Israel honored himself today" (6:20).
- David: "**I will make myself yet more contemptible** … by them I shall be held in honor" (6:21–22).
- "Michal … had no child to the day of her death" (6:23).
- **Heart and way:** "**Consider** [*set your heart on*] **your ways**" (Hag 1:5, 7) → §4.1
- **Spirit, not might:** "**Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit**" (Zec 4:6) [D1]

- **Hardened against the Spirit's words:** "They made their **hearts diamond-hard** lest they should hear … the words that the Lord of hosts had sent **by his Spirit** through the former prophets" (Zec 7:12) [D1]
- **Testing heart and mind; vengeance:** Jer 11:20; 20:12 → §6.1
- **Guarding the spirit:** Mal 2:16 → §5.1
- **Taking to heart:** "if you will not **take it to heart** … because you **do not lay it to heart**" (Mal 2:2)
- **Words eaten, heart delighted:** "Your words were found, and **I ate them**, and your words became to me a joy and **the delight of my heart**" (Jer 15:16)
- **Visions of one's own mind:** "They speak visions of **their own minds**, not from the mouth of the Lord" (Jer 23:16)
- **God's own nephesh as oath:** "The Lord of hosts **has sworn by himself** [*his nephesh*]" (Jer 51:14; Amo 6:8) → Batch D, Batch E; Batch G §4 (§R-V)
- "surrender … **your life shall be spared**" (Jer 38:17)
- "they seek **my life**, to take it away" (1Ki 19:10, 14)
- "Why do you commit this great evil **against yourselves**?" (Jer 44:7)
- "your servant has **found courage** [*his heart*] **to pray**" (2Sa 7:27)
- "the clans of Judah shall **say to themselves**" (Zec 12:5)
- "creates **the wind**, and **declares to man what is his thought**" (Amo 4:13)
- "I will remove … **the spirit of uncleanness**" (Zec 13:2) [O+X]
- "stirred up **the spirit** of Zerubbabel … Joshua … and all the remnant" (Hag 1:14) → G §11
- "eat **the flesh**" (Jer 7:21)
- "Let her **lie in your arms** [*bosom*], that my lord the king may be warm" (1Ki 1:2) — the king's failing body (G §8)

- "everyone who was in distress … and everyone who was **bitter in soul**, gathered to him. And **he became commander** over them" (1Sa 22:2) — **bitterness of soul as the recruiting ground of a future king**
- "With him is **an arm of flesh**, but with us is the Lord … And the people **took confidence**" (2Ch 32:8), spoken "encouragingly [*to their heart*]" (32:6)
- "**fatter in flesh** than all the youths who ate **the king's food**" (Dan 1:15) → §7.6
- "the gods, whose dwelling is **not with flesh**" (Dan 2:11)
- "**Our flesh is as the flesh of our brothers** … yet we are forcing our sons … to be slaves … it is **not in our power** to help it" (Neh 5:5) → §3
- "the kings … **their hearts melted and there was no longer any spirit in them**" (Jos 5:1) [H2]
- "**the souls** of those who had been beheaded … **came to life and reigned** with Christ" (Rev 20:4)
- "the king … had **sackcloth beneath on his body**" (2Ki 6:30) — hidden grief under royal clothes
- "**your heart has become proud in your wealth**" (Eze 28:5)
- "Beware lest you **say in your heart**, 'My power and the might of my hand have gotten me this wealth'" (Deu 8:17)
- "if riches increase, **set not your heart on them**" (Psa 62:10)
- "you did not serve the Lord … with **gladness of heart**, because of **the abundance of all things**" (Deu 28:47)
- "**your heart shall thrill and exult**, because … **the wealth of the nations** shall come to you" (Isa 60:5)
- "he did with all his heart, and **prospered**" (2Ch 31:21)
- **Wealth not asked for:** "Because **this was in your heart**, and you have not asked for possessions, wealth, honor, or **the life** of those who hate you" (2Ch 1:11; 1Ki 3:11)
- **◆ Wealth does not satisfy a heart set on a grievance.** Context read: Est 5:9–14.
- Haman goes out "**joyful and glad of heart**", sees Mordecai, and is "filled with wrath" (5:9).
- He "recounted … **the splendor of his riches**, the number of his sons, all the promotions" (5:11). Then: "**Yet all this is worth nothing to me**, so long as I see Mordecai" (5:13).
- The gallows follow (5:14).

[Claude reading] The same wealth thrills the heart (Isa 60), makes it proud (Eze 28) and is claimed by it as its own work (Deu 8). The relation depends on **whether the heart sets itself on the wealth** (Psa 62:10) or on the one who gives it. Haman shows a third case: **wealth recited to a heart that is fixed on an injury gives no comfort.**
- "**The ransom of a man's life is his wealth**, but a poor man hears no threat" (Pro 13:8)
- "each shall give **a ransom for his life** … **The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less** … to make atonement for your lives" (Exo 30:12–16; context read) → Batch D; Batch E
- "your life shall be for his life, **or else you shall pay a talent of silver**" (1Ki 20:39) → §1.4
- Satan: "**Skin for skin! All that a man has he will give for his life**" (Job 2:4) → "only **spare** [*guard*] **his life**" (2:6). Context read: Job 2:3–7.
- "they have **devoured human lives**; they have **taken treasure**" (Eze 22:25)
[Claude reading] Batch G §5.4 read Mic 6:7 and Mat 16:26 as a refusal to set any price on the soul. **This batch shows the law and the narratives do set a price, and state it:**
- a ransom in wealth (Pro 13:8)
- a half-shekel that is **equal for every life** (Exo 30:15)
- a talent of silver in a parable that turns into "life for life" (1Ki 20:39–42)

Satan's axiom (Job 2:4) is that **a man will give everything for his *nephesh***. The difference from G §5.4 is the direction of the transaction: **a life can be ransomed within the covenant, but a soul cannot be bought back from God** (Mat 16:26). See §R-V.
- "the **soul** of the diligent **is richly supplied** [*made fat*]" (Pro 13:4)
- "**Whoever brings blessing** [*the soul of blessing*] **will be enriched** [*made fat*]" (Pro 11:25) [lexical: *dāšēn* H1878]
- **Heart made fat = dull:** "**Make the heart of this people dull** [*fat*] … lest they … understand with their hearts" (Isa 6:10) [lexical: *šāman* H8080]
- **Flesh:** "the **fat of his flesh will grow lean**" (Isa 17:4). "**fatter in flesh**" on vegetables (Dan 1:15).
- "according to **the riches of his glory** he may grant you to be **strengthened with power through his Spirit in your inner being**" (Eph 3:16) [D1]
- "having **the eyes of your hearts** enlightened, that you may know … **the riches of his glorious inheritance**" (Eph 1:18)
- "that **their hearts** may be encouraged … to reach all **the riches of full assurance** of understanding" (Col 2:2)
- "Let the word of Christ **dwell in you richly** … singing … **spiritual** songs, with thankfulness **in your hearts**" (Col 3:16)
- "**The fruit for which your soul longed** has gone from you, and all your delicacies and your splendors are lost" (Rev 18:14)
- Simon's money for the Spirit (Act 8:18; §1.6)

- **The queen of Sheba** "told him **all that was on her mind**" (1Ki 10:2; 2Ch 9:1). After seeing Solomon's house and table, "**there was no more breath [*spirit*] in her**" (1Ki 10:5; context read; see Batch E). **What she heard filled her mind; what she saw took her spirit away.**
- "**my heart moans for Moab like a flute** … Therefore **the riches they gained have perished**" (Jer 48:36) — grief of heart over an enemy's lost wealth
- "The soul of the sluggard **craves and gets nothing**" (Pro 13:4); "his eyes are never satisfied with riches … '**For whom am I toiling and depriving myself** [*my soul*] of pleasure?'" (Ecc 4:8)
- "When **the cares of my heart are many**, your consolations **cheer my soul**" (Psa 94:19) — abundance of cares answered by consolation
- "**Our soul has had more than enough** of the scorn of those who are **at ease**" (Psa 123:4)
- "Bondservants, obey your **earthly** [*according to the flesh*] masters … **with a sincere heart**, as you would Christ" (Eph 6:5)
- "not by the way of **eye-service** … but as bondservants of Christ, **doing the will of God from the heart** [*soul*]" (Eph 6:6)
- "not by way of eye-service … but with **sincerity of heart**" (Col 3:22)
- "no longer as a bondservant … as a beloved brother … **both in the flesh and in the Lord**" (Phile 16)
- "you who were once **slaves of sin** have become **obedient from the heart**" (Rom 6:17). Context 6:16–18: "you are slaves of the one whom you obey".
- "present your members as **slaves to righteousness**" (Rom 6:19)
- "**I myself serve the law of God with my mind, but with my flesh I serve the law of sin**" (Rom 7:25)
- "we **serve in the new way of the Spirit**" (Rom 7:6) [D3]
- "you did not receive **the spirit of slavery to fall back into fear**, but … **the Spirit of adoption**" (Rom 8:15) [X+D1]
- "do not use your freedom as an opportunity **for the flesh**, but through love **serve one another**" (Gal 5:13)
- "fervent **in spirit**, serve the Lord" (Rom 12:11) [H1]
- "such persons do not serve our Lord Christ, but **their own appetites** [*belly*], and … **deceive the hearts** of the naive" (Rom 16:18)

[Claude reading] **In the NT, slavery is described by which component does the serving.** A social slave can serve "from the heart", and so is free where it matters. A free man can be a slave in his flesh (Rom 7:25). **The "spirit of slavery" is a spirit of fear** (Rom 8:15), which links this batch to Batch A. *kata sarka* "according to the flesh" (Eph 6:5) marks the social relation as the **flesh-level** one. Phile 16 holds both levels at once.

"if that servant **says to himself** [*in his heart*], '**My master is delayed**,' and begins to beat the … servants, and **to eat and drink and get drunk**" (Luk 12:45; Mat 24:48–49). Context read: Luk 12:42–46; Mat 24:49–51.
- The faithful manager feeds the household "at the proper time" (Luk 12:42).

- **God's soul burdened:** "Your new moons and your appointed feasts **my soul hates; they have become a burden to me; I am weary of bearing them**" (Isa 1:14). Context 1:13–15: "I will hide my eyes … your hands are full of blood".
- **Moses' burden, then the Spirit shared.** Context read: Num 11:10–17.
- "it has **seemed good to the Holy Spirit** and to us to lay on you **no greater burden**" (Act 15:28) [D1]
- "they cannot save **the burden**, but **themselves** [*their nephesh*] **go into captivity**" (Isa 46:2) — the idols, which have to be carried, and their carriers
- "**Take care for the sake of your lives**, and do not bear a burden on the Sabbath" (Jer 17:21) → §5.1

- **The soul's "burden" is its desire.** "the delight of their eyes and **their soul's desire** [*the lifting up of their soul*]" (Eze 24:25). [lexical] *maśśāʾ* H4853 is both "burden" and "that to which the soul lifts itself". **The noun for a load is the noun for longing.**

- "**on my male servants and female servants** … I will pour out **my Spirit**" (Act 2:18); "**slaves or free** … all were made to drink of **one Spirit**" (1Co 12:13) — the Spirit does not follow social rank
- "the flesh of all men, **both free and slave**" (Rev 19:18) — the same end for both
- "I am **a fellow servant** with you … the testimony of Jesus is **the spirit of prophecy**" (Rev 19:10) [U]
- "**direct your heart in the way**" (Pro 23:19)
- "My son, **give me your heart**, and let your eyes observe my ways" (Pro 23:26)
- "he went on backsliding **in the way of his own heart**" (Isa 57:17)
- "**Walk in the ways of your heart** and the sight of your eyes. **But know** that … God will bring you into judgment" (Ecc 11:9) → Batch F §7.4
- "if … **my heart has gone after my eyes**" (Job 31:7)
- "I will give them **one heart and one way**" (Jer 32:39)
- "I will **run in the way** of your commandments **when you enlarge my heart**" (Psa 119:32)
- "**Teach me your way** … **unite my heart** to fear your name" (Psa 86:11)
- **Set the heart on the ways:** "**Consider** [*set your heart on*] **your ways**" (Hag 1:5, 7) — the prophet's summons is for the heart to look at the way
- "All the ways of a man are pure in his own eyes, but **the Lord weighs the spirit**" (Pro 16:2) [H2]
- "Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but **the Lord weighs the heart**" (Pro 21:2)
- "I the Lord **search the heart** … to give every man **according to his ways**" (Jer 17:10); "render to each **whose heart you know, according to all his ways**" (2Ch 6:30)
- **The heart blames God for the ruined way:** "When a man's folly **brings his way to ruin**, **his heart rages against the Lord**" (Pro 19:3)
- **"Lifted up" in the Lord's ways:** "**His heart was courageous** [*lifted up*] **in the ways of the Lord**" (2Ch 17:6) → Batch D (the "high heart", pride or courage by direction)

[Claude reading] The relation runs in both directions. The heart can lead the way (Pro 23:19), be dragged by the eyes (Job 31:7), or go its own way (Isa 57:17). The best state is **one heart with one way** (Jer 32:39), **enlarged** so that the way can be run (Psa 119:32). **Eyes judge the way; God weighs the heart or spirit behind it** (Pro 16:2; 21:2).
1. **The heart itself:** "a people who **go astray in their heart**" (Psa 95:10)
2. **The spirit, with a way back:** "those who **go astray in spirit will come to understanding**" (Isa 29:24) [H1]
- "**a spirit of whoredom has led them astray**" (Hos 4:12) [X]
- "The Lord has **mingled within her a spirit of confusion** … as **a drunken man staggers**" (Isa 19:14) [X]

4. **God:** "O Lord, **why do you make us wander from your ways and harden our heart**?" (Isa 63:17). [Claude reading] In the text the king's heart is the heart with the most power over others. It is also the heart shown most often as acted upon: God turns it, puts things into it, stirs it, hardens it, and cuts it off. The unsearchable heart of Pro 25:3 is unsearchable to subjects. To God it is a stream in his hand.

1.2 The heart that claims a throne: "You said in your heart, 'I will ascend to heaven … I will set my throne on high'" (Isa 14:13); "in his own mind he shall become great … he shall even rise up against the Prince of princes" (Dan 8:25); "in her heart she says, 'I sit as a queen, I am no widow'" (Rev 18:7); "the arrogant heart of the king of Assyria" (Isa 10:12); "Your heart was proud because of your beauty … I exposed you before kings" (Eze 28:17); "when his heart was lifted up and his spirit was hardened … he was brought down from his kingly throne" (Dan 5:20). Then "his mind was made like that of a beast … until he knew that the Most High God rules the kingdom of mankind" (5:21). See Batch G §14.10.
The remedy in the law of the king: he is to write out the law and "read in it all the days of his life … that his heart may not be lifted up above his brothers" (Deu 17:19–20).

The subject's version: "Haman said to himself [*in his heart*], 'Whom would the king delight to honor more than me?'" (Est 6:6). Context 6:7–12: he describes the honour, is made to give it to Mordecai, and "hurried to his house, mourning and with his head covered" (6:12).

1.2 The heart that claims a throne: [Claude reading] Isa 14, Dan 8 and Rev 18 all use the same form: the heart speaks a claim to rule, and the fall follows. Deu 17 gives the only preventive, and it is a daily one: reading, so that the heart is not raised. Haman's inner sentence is the courtier's form of the same claim, and the reversal follows within the same scene.

What the sequence shows [Claude reading]: Allegiance is a heart-matter, and it moves by attention. Absalom wins hearts by standing where the king is absent (15:2–4) and by the kiss the king himself gave him (14:33 → 15:5). The heart follows whoever hears the cause.; The king's own heart drives the plot. The heart that "went out to Absalom" (14:1) opens the way for the son who steals every other heart. After the victory the same heart grieves, and nearly loses the army (19:6–7).; Flesh as a claim on the heart. David recovers Judah's heart with "bone and flesh" — kinship offered as grounds for allegiance.; The same claim in the opposite direction: Abimelech — "Remember also that I am your bone and your flesh" (Judg 9:2) → "their hearts inclined to follow Abimelech, for they said, 'He is our brother'" (9:3) → he kills his seventy brothers "on one stone" (9:5).; One appeal to kinship-flesh wins hearts for restoration in one case and for fratricide in the other. [Claude reading]

findings.text: A spirit as someone's income: "a slave girl who had a spirit of divination and brought her owners much gain" (Act 16:16) [O]

1.6 Authority over spirits — who commands whom: "the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that is now at work in the sons of disobedience" (Eph 2:2) [O]; [Claude reading] Here spirit sits beside authority and money. Spirits obey Jesus; a spirit overpowers those who borrow his name; the Spirit cannot be bought, and the attempt exposes the heart; a spirit is exploited for profit. In each case the question is who has authority over which spirit.

1.7 Kingdom — spirit, flesh, heart, soul (NT): "unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom" (Joh 3:5) [D3]; "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom" (Mat 5:3) [H1]; "if it is by the Spirit of God that I cast out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you" (Mat 12:28); "the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking but of … joy in the Holy Spirit" (Rom 14:17) → §7.6; "flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom" (1Co 15:50); "strengthening the souls of the disciples … through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom" (Act 14:22); "hears the word of the kingdom … the evil one snatches away what has been sown in his heart" (Mat 13:19)

Two flights to Achish, both begun in the heart.; Context 1Sa 21:10–15: the servants of Achish recall the song → "David took these words to heart and was much afraid of Achish" (12) → he feigns madness (13).; Context 1Sa 26:21–27:4. Saul's oath comes first: "I will no more do you harm, because my life was precious in your eyes this day. Behold, I have acted foolishly, and have made a great mistake" (26:21). David: "as your life was precious this day in my sight, so may my life be precious in the sight of the Lord" (26:24). Saul: "Blessed be you, my son David!" (26:25).; Immediately after: "Then David said in his heart, 'Now I shall perish one day by the hand of Saul'" (27:1) → he goes back to Achish (27:2) → "he no longer sought him" (27:4).; [Claude reading] David does not answer Saul's promise with trust. He answers it by putting his life in the Lord's sight (26:24) and then with a private sentence in his heart that the promise will fail. The heart's reading of the king proves right: Saul stops only when David is out of reach. This adds context to the "said in heart" series (depiction v1 §2.1c; Batch B §0).

"Michal … saw King David leaping and dancing … and she despised him in her heart" (2Sa 6:16; 1Ch 15:29).; After: it becomes speech — "How the king of Israel honored himself today" (6:20).; David: "I will make myself yet more contemptible … by them I shall be held in honor" (6:21–22).; "Michal … had no child to the day of her death" (6:23).; Heart-contempt → speech → a permanent sequel. See Batch C.

Hardened against the Spirit's words: "They made their hearts diamond-hard lest they should hear … the words that the Lord of hosts had sent by his Spirit through the former prophets" (Zec 7:12) [D1]

Life: "surrender … your life shall be spared" (Jer 38:17); "they seek my life, to take it away" (1Ki 19:10, 14); "Why do you commit this great evil against yourselves?" (Jer 44:7)

Other: "your servant has found courage [*his heart*] to pray" (2Sa 7:27); "the clans of Judah shall say to themselves" (Zec 12:5); "creates the wind, and declares to man what is his thought" (Amo 4:13); "I will remove … the spirit of uncleanness" (Zec 13:2) [O+X]; "stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel … Joshua … and all the remnant" (Hag 1:14) → G §11; "eat the flesh" (Jer 7:21)

1.10 ◆ Fringe (M72): "Let her lie in your arms [*bosom*], that my lord the king may be warm" (1Ki 1:2) — the king's failing body (G §8); "everyone who was in distress … and everyone who was bitter in soul, gathered to him. And he became commander over them" (1Sa 22:2) — bitterness of soul as the recruiting ground of a future king; "With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the Lord … And the people took confidence" (2Ch 32:8), spoken "encouragingly [*to their heart*]" (32:6); "fatter in flesh than all the youths who ate the king's food" (Dan 1:15) → §7.6; "the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh" (Dan 2:11); "Our flesh is as the flesh of our brothers … yet we are forcing our sons … to be slaves … it is not in our power to help it" (Neh 5:5) → §3; "the kings … their hearts melted and there was no longer any spirit in them" (Jos 5:1) [H2]; "the souls of those who had been beheaded … came to life and reigned with Christ" (Rev 20:4); "the king … had sackcloth beneath on his body" (2Ki 6:30) — hidden grief under royal clothes

Negative: "your heart has become proud in your wealth" (Eze 28:5); "Beware lest you say in your heart, 'My power and the might of my hand have gotten me this wealth'" (Deu 8:17); "if riches increase, set not your heart on them" (Psa 62:10); "you did not serve the Lord … with gladness of heart, because of the abundance of all things" (Deu 28:47)
Positive: "your heart shall thrill and exult, because … the wealth of the nations shall come to you" (Isa 60:5); "he did with all his heart, and prospered" (2Ch 31:21)
Wealth not asked for: "Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked for possessions, wealth, honor, or the life of those who hate you" (2Ch 1:11; 1Ki 3:11)

Wealth does not satisfy a heart set on a grievance. Context read: Est 5:9–14.; Haman goes out "joyful and glad of heart", sees Mordecai, and is "filled with wrath" (5:9).; He "recounted … the splendor of his riches, the number of his sons, all the promotions" (5:11). Then: "Yet all this is worth nothing to me, so long as I see Mordecai" (5:13).; The gallows follow (5:14).

findings.text: 2.1 Heart and riches — the value depends on where the heart is set: [Claude reading] The same wealth thrills the heart (Isa 60), makes it proud (Eze 28) and is claimed by it as its own work (Deu 8). The relation depends on whether the heart sets itself on the wealth (Psa 62:10) or on the one who gives it. Haman shows a third case: wealth recited to a heart that is fixed on an injury gives no comfort.

2.2 The price of a life, again: "The ransom of a man's life is his wealth, but a poor man hears no threat" (Pro 13:8); "each shall give a ransom for his life … The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less … to make atonement for your lives" (Exo 30:12–16; context read) → Batch D; Batch E; "your life shall be for his life, or else you shall pay a talent of silver" (1Ki 20:39) → §1.4; Satan: "Skin for skin! All that a man has he will give for his life" (Job 2:4) → "only spare [*guard*] his life" (2:6). Context read: Job 2:3–7.; "they have devoured human lives; they have taken treasure" (Eze 22:25); [Claude reading] Batch G §5.4 read Mic 6:7 and Mat 16:26 as a refusal to set any price on the soul. This batch shows the law and the narratives do set a price, and state it: a ransom in wealth (Pro 13:8); a half-shekel that is equal for every life (Exo 30:15); a talent of silver in a parable that turns into "life for life" (1Ki 20:39–42); Satan's axiom (Job 2:4) is that a man will give everything for his *nephesh*. The difference from G §5.4 is the direction of the transaction: a life can be ransomed within the covenant, but a soul cannot be bought back from God (Mat 16:26). See §R-V.

findings.text: Soul made fat = satisfied: "the soul of the diligent is richly supplied [*made fat*]" (Pro 13:4); "Whoever brings blessing [*the soul of blessing*] will be enriched [*made fat*]" (Pro 11:25) [lexical: *dāšēn* H1878]
Heart made fat = dull: "Make the heart of this people dull [*fat*] … lest they … understand with their hearts" (Isa 6:10) [lexical: *šāman* H8080]
Flesh: "the fat of his flesh will grow lean" (Isa 17:4). "fatter in flesh" on vegetables (Dan 1:15).

2.4 Riches moved inward (NT): "according to the riches of his glory he may grant you to be strengthened with power through his Spirit in your inner being" (Eph 3:16) [D1]; "having the eyes of your hearts enlightened, that you may know … the riches of his glorious inheritance" (Eph 1:18); "that their hearts may be encouraged … to reach all the riches of full assurance of understanding" (Col 2:2); "Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly … singing … spiritual songs, with thankfulness in your hearts" (Col 3:16)
The reverse: "The fruit for which your soul longed has gone from you, and all your delicacies and your splendors are lost" (Rev 18:14); Simon's money for the Spirit (Act 8:18; §1.6)

The queen of Sheba "told him all that was on her mind" (1Ki 10:2; 2Ch 9:1). After seeing Solomon's house and table, "there was no more breath [*spirit*] in her" (1Ki 10:5; context read; see Batch E). What she heard filled her mind; what she saw took her spirit away.

2.5 ◆ Fringe (M46): "my heart moans for Moab like a flute … Therefore the riches they gained have perished" (Jer 48:36) — grief of heart over an enemy's lost wealth; "The soul of the sluggard craves and gets nothing" (Pro 13:4); "his eyes are never satisfied with riches … 'For whom am I toiling and depriving myself [*my soul*] of pleasure?'" (Ecc 4:8); "When the cares of my heart are many, your consolations cheer my soul" (Psa 94:19) — abundance of cares answered by consolation; "Our soul has had more than enough of the scorn of those who are at ease" (Psa 123:4)

The slave serves from the heart: "Bondservants, obey your earthly [*according to the flesh*] masters … with a sincere heart, as you would Christ" (Eph 6:5); "not by the way of eye-service … but as bondservants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart [*soul*]" (Eph 6:6); "not by way of eye-service … but with sincerity of heart" (Col 3:22)
3.1 Service located in a component: "no longer as a bondservant … as a beloved brother … both in the flesh and in the Lord" (Phile 16)

Slavery transferred inward: "you who were once slaves of sin have become obedient from the heart" (Rom 6:17). Context 6:16–18: "you are slaves of the one whom you obey".; "present your members as slaves to righteousness" (Rom 6:19); "I myself serve the law of God with my mind, but with my flesh I serve the law of sin" (Rom 7:25); "we serve in the new way of the Spirit" (Rom 7:6) [D3]; "you did not receive the spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but … the Spirit of adoption" (Rom 8:15) [X+D1]; "do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another" (Gal 5:13); "fervent in spirit, serve the Lord" (Rom 12:11) [H1]; "such persons do not serve our Lord Christ, but their own appetites [*belly*], and … deceive the hearts of the naive" (Rom 16:18)

3.1 Service located in a component: [Claude reading] In the NT, slavery is described by which component does the serving. A social slave can serve "from the heart", and so is free where it matters. A free man can be a slave in his flesh (Rom 7:25). The "spirit of slavery" is a spirit of fear (Rom 8:15), which links this batch to Batch A. *kata sarka* "according to the flesh" (Eph 6:5) marks the social relation as the flesh-level one. Phile 16 holds both levels at once.

3.2 The servant's inner sentence: "if that servant says to himself [*in his heart*], 'My master is delayed,' and begins to beat the … servants, and to eat and drink and get drunk" (Luk 12:45; Mat 24:48–49). Context read: Luk 12:42–46; Mat 24:49–51.; The faithful manager feeds the household "at the proper time" (Luk 12:42).; The unfaithful servant says in his heart that the master is delayed → beats → eats and drinks with drunkards → the master "will come on a day when he does not expect him" (46).; → Batch D §10 (inner speech). New here: the inner sentence is followed at once by eating and drinking, then the sudden arrival (§7.6).

findings.text: 3.3 Burden — who bears it: "it has seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to lay on you no greater burden" (Act 15:28) [D1]; "they cannot save the burden, but themselves [*their nephesh*] go into captivity" (Isa 46:2) — the idols, which have to be carried, and their carriers; "Take care for the sake of your lives, and do not bear a burden on the Sabbath" (Jer 17:21) → §5.1

The soul's "burden" is its desire. "the delight of their eyes and their soul's desire [*the lifting up of their soul*]" (Eze 24:25). [lexical] *maśśāʾ* H4853 is both "burden" and "that to which the soul lifts itself". The noun for a load is the noun for longing.

3.4 ◆ Fringe (M78): "on my male servants and female servants … I will pour out my Spirit" (Act 2:18); "slaves or free … all were made to drink of one Spirit" (1Co 12:13) — the Spirit does not follow social rank; "the flesh of all men, both free and slave" (Rev 19:18) — the same end for both; "I am a fellow servant with you … the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy" (Rev 19:10) [U]
The heart directs the way: "direct your heart in the way" (Pro 23:19); "My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes observe my ways" (Pro 23:26)

The way follows the heart: "he went on backsliding in the way of his own heart" (Isa 57:17); "Walk in the ways of your heart and the sight of your eyes. But know that … God will bring you into judgment" (Ecc 11:9) → Batch F §7.4; "if … my heart has gone after my eyes" (Job 31:7)

Heart and way given together: "I will give them one heart and one way" (Jer 32:39); "I will run in the way of your commandments when you enlarge my heart" (Psa 119:32); "Teach me your way … unite my heart to fear your name" (Psa 86:11)
Set the heart on the ways: "Consider [*set your heart on*] your ways" (Hag 1:5, 7) — the prophet's summons is for the heart to look at the way

Weighing: "All the ways of a man are pure in his own eyes, but the Lord weighs the spirit" (Pro 16:2) [H2]; "Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the Lord weighs the heart" (Pro 21:2); "I the Lord search the heart … to give every man according to his ways" (Jer 17:10); "render to each whose heart you know, according to all his ways" (2Ch 6:30)
The heart blames God for the ruined way: "When a man's folly brings his way to ruin, his heart rages against the Lord" (Pro 19:3)
"Lifted up" in the Lord's ways: "His heart was courageous [*lifted up*] in the ways of the Lord" (2Ch 17:6) → Batch D (the "high heart", pride or courage by direction)

4.1 Heart and way — which leads?: [Claude reading] The relation runs in both directions. The heart can lead the way (Pro 23:19), be dragged by the eyes (Job 31:7), or go its own way (Isa 57:17). The best state is one heart with one way (Jer 32:39), enlarged so that the way can be run (Psa 119:32). Eyes judge the way; God weighs the heart or spirit behind it (Pro 16:2; 21:2).

4.2 Going astray — five agents: The heart itself: "a people who go astray in their heart" (Psa 95:10); The spirit, with a way back: "those who go astray in spirit will come to understanding" (Isa 29:24) [H1]; A foreign spirit: "a spirit of whoredom has led them astray" (Hos 4:12) [X]; "The Lord has mingled within her a spirit of confusion … as a drunken man staggers" (Isa 19:14) [X]; God: "O Lord, why do you make us wander from your ways and harden our heart?" (Isa 63:17). Context 63:1–6, 15–17: this complaint follows the divine warrior's "day of vengeance was in my heart" (63:4) and a plea that "the stirring of your inner parts and your compassion are held back" (63:15). → §6.1; The loss of understanding: "He takes away understanding [*heart*] from the chiefs … and makes them wander in a trackless waste" (Job 12:24)
Unwitting error: "the person [*nephesh*] who makes a mistake, when he sins unintentionally" (Num 15:28) — atonement is provided
A confession that is not trusted: Saul: "I have acted foolishly, and have made a great mistake" (1Sa 26:21) → David still flees (§1.8)
Intoxication: "Why should you be intoxicated, my son, with a forbidden woman" (Pro 5:20). The verse before uses the same verb for the wife: "be intoxicated always in her love" (5:19) [verify].

4.2 Going astray — five agents: The same verb covers the innocent slip, a king's self-accusation and erotic absorption. In each the self is carried off course without full deliberation.; "My heart staggers; horror has appalled me; the twilight I longed for has been turned for me into trembling" (Isa 21:4). Context 21:1–4: a stern vision "as whirlwinds … sweep on"; "my loins are filled with anguish … I am bowed down so that I cannot hear". The prophet's own heart reels from the vision it received.; "his breath is like an overflowing stream … a bridle that leads astray" (Isa 30:28) — God's breath as the thing that sends the nations astray; "all flesh had corrupted their way" (Gen 6:12) → G §1.3

4.3 Guarding the way keeps the soul: "whoever guards his way preserves his life" (Pro 16:17); "Whoever keeps the commandment keeps his life; he who despises his ways will die" (Pro 19:16); "Thorns and snares are in the way of the crooked; whoever guards his soul will keep far from them" (Pro 22:5); The watchman: "if you warn the wicked to turn from his way … you will have delivered your soul" (Eze 3:19; 33:9) → §5.2

Others address my soul: "how can you say to my soul, 'Flee like a bird to your mountain'" (Psa 11:1). Context 11:2: "the wicked bend the bow … to shoot … at the upright in heart". → Batch E. Counter-voice to the self-address: here others speak to the soul, urging flight, and the psalmist refuses (§7.8).

4.4 ◆ Fringe (M76): "Reproaches have broken my heart … I looked for pity [*someone to shake the head*], but there was none" (Psa 69:20); "you have disheartened the righteous falsely" (Eze 13:22) → G §5.3; "they have chosen their own ways, and their soul delights in their abominations" (Isa 66:3); "Your ways and your deeds … it has reached your very heart" (Jer 4:18) — the consequence of the way arrives at the heart; "The dogs have a mighty appetite [*nephesh*] … they have all turned to their own way" (Isa 56:11); "Ephraim feeds on the wind" (Hos 12:1)

5.1 Guarding one's own inner seat: "Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life" (Pro 4:23). Context 4:20–27 — the guarding moves outward: words kept "within your heart" (21) → "life … and healing to all their flesh" (22); keep the heart (23); → the mouth: "put away … crooked speech" (24); → the eyes: "look directly forward" (25); → the feet: "Ponder the path of your feet" (26–27); "take care, and keep your soul diligently, lest you forget … lest they depart from your heart" (Deu 4:9) — guarding the soul means guarding memory; "guard yourselves in your spirit, and let none of you be faithless to the wife of your youth" (Mal 2:15–16) [U+H1; H1]; "watch yourselves lest your hearts be weighed down with dissipation and drunkenness" (Luk 21:34) → §7.6; "restore him in a spirit of gentleness. Keep watch on yourself" (Gal 6:1) [X]; "Take care lest there be an unworthy thought in your heart" (Deu 15:9); "Take care lest your heart be deceived" (Deu 11:16); "Be very careful, therefore [*guard well your souls*], to love the Lord" (Jos 23:11) — distance 0: the "careful" word *is* the nephesh phrase

The opposite sense of the same verb — *nāṣar* [lexical; Claude reading]: "Keep [*nāṣar*] your heart with all vigilance" (Pro 4:23); "the woman meets him, dressed as a prostitute, wily [*nāṣar*, guarded] of heart" (Pro 7:10). Context 7:11–12: "loud and wayward … at every corner she lies in wait".

A guarded heart is the wise man's protection in Pro 4 and the seductress's concealment in Pro 7. The same verb, in the same book, three chapters apart. Candidate for the synthesis item "one word, opposite value" (§7.4).

5.3 Keeping something in the heart — holding what is not yet understood: Daniel: "my thoughts greatly alarmed me, and my color changed, but I kept the matter in my heart" (Dan 7:28) → Batch B; Batch G; Mary: after the shepherds: "treasured up all these things, pondering them in her heart" (Luk 2:19); after the temple, where "they did not understand the saying" (2:50): "his mother treasured up all these things in her heart" (2:51); "keep them within your heart" (Pro 4:21); [Claude reading] "Keeping in the heart" follows alarm (Daniel) or incomprehension (Mary, 2:50). The heart holds what the mind cannot yet resolve. In both cases the keeping is the end of the scene: nothing is said or done yet.

Eli. Context read: 1Sa 4:12–18.; "Eli was sitting on his seat by the road watching, for his heart trembled for the ark of God" (13); The report: Israel fled, "Your two sons also … are dead, and the ark of God has been captured" (17); "As soon as he mentioned the ark of God, Eli fell over backward … and he died" (18); [Claude reading] The heart's fear was for the ark, and it is the ark, not the sons, that kills him. What the heart watches for decides which word is fatal.

God's heart | "the day of vengeance was in my heart, and my year of redemption had come" (Isa 63:4). Context 63:1–6: "I have trodden the winepress alone … I looked, but there was no one to help … so my own arm brought me salvation".
God's nephesh | "shall I not avenge myself [*shall not my soul avenge itself*] on a nation such as this?" (Jer 5:9, 29; 9:9) → Batch E
The persecuted prophet | "O Lord of hosts, who tests the righteous, who sees the heart and the mind, let me see your vengeance upon them, for to you have I committed my cause" (Jer 20:12; 11:20)
The nations' soul | "the Philistines … took vengeance with malice of soul" (Eze 25:15) → Batch E, F, G
The anxious heart, comforted | "Say to those who have an anxious heart, 'Be strong; fear not! Behold, your God will come with vengeance … He will come and save you'" (Isa 35:4)
A stirred human spirit, as instrument | "The Lord has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes … that is the vengeance of the Lord" (Jer 51:11) [H1]

Jeremiah's sequence — context read, Jer 20:7–14: "you have deceived me" (7); "there is in my heart as it were a burning fire shut up in my bones … I cannot [hold it in]" (9); "my close friends, watching for my fall … 'take our revenge on him'" (10); → "let me see your vengeance … to you have I committed my cause" (12); → "Sing to the Lord; praise the Lord! For he has delivered the life of the needy" (13); → "Cursed be the day on which I was born!" (14); Jer 11:18–21 has the same prayer, and names "the men of Anathoth, who seek your life" (21).; [Claude reading]; Vengeance changes value with the heart that holds it. In the Philistines' soul it is malice. In God's heart it stands in one line with redemption (Isa 63:4). To the anxious heart it is rescue (Isa 35:4).; The prophet's heart does not take vengeance; it hands vengeance over. The friends want "our revenge" (20:10). Jeremiah asks to *see* God's (20:12). The handing over ("to you have I committed my cause") is what makes the praise of 20:13 possible. Two verses later the heart falls to cursing its birth (20:14). The inner seat swings from fire, to entrusting, to praise, to despair in five verses (cf. the despairing soul, Batch G §6).; What follows the divine heart's vengeance is complaint (Isa 63:15–17): the people ask where God's compassion has gone and why he makes them wander (§4.2).

findings.text: 6.2 The heart as judge of the self: "Faithless Israel has shown herself [*her nephesh*] more righteous than treacherous Judah" (Jer 3:11) — comparative justification; "I do not say this to condemn you, for … you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together" (2Co 7:3); [Claude reading] The heart can condemn the self (1Jo 3:20) or justify it (Job 32:2; Luk 16:15). In both cases the text places a higher court above it: "God is greater than our heart"; "God knows your hearts". 1Jo 3 is the gentler reading: the self-condemning heart is reassured, not overruled harshly. In 2Co 7:3 condemnation is set aside because the other person is held in the heart.

findings.text: 6.3 Flesh and justification: "by works of the law no human being [*flesh*] will be justified" (Rom 3:20; Gal 2:16); "God has done what the law, weakened by the flesh, could not do … in the likeness of sinful flesh … he condemned sin in the flesh" (Rom 8:3); "manifested in the flesh, vindicated by the Spirit" (1Ti 3:16) [U]; "you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God" (1Co 6:11) [D1]; "unnatural desire [*other flesh*] … undergoing a punishment of eternal fire" (Jude 7); [Claude reading] Within this cluster *flesh* means three things: all humanity, which cannot be justified; the place where sin is condemned; and Christ's own flesh, which is vindicated by the Spirit. This extends Batch G §7 (flesh valued by circumstance).

6.4 Counting: "So teach us to number our days that we may get a heart of wisdom" (Psa 90:12) → Batch B; "he poured out his soul to death and was numbered with the transgressors" (Isa 53:12); "Out of the anguish of his soul he shall see and be satisfied … make many to be accounted righteous" (53:11); "it is not the children of the flesh who are the children of God, but the children of the promise are counted as offspring" (Rom 9:8)
Balaam: "Who can count the dust of Jacob …? Let me [*my nephesh*] die the death of the upright" (Num 23:10) — the hired curser's soul wishes for the end of those he was hired to curse

Shared threat as shelter. Context read: 1Sa 22:20–23. "I have occasioned the death of all the persons of your father's house" (22) → "Stay with me … for he who seeks my life seeks your life. With me you shall be in safekeeping" (23). David's guilt becomes a pledge: the one threat to both lives becomes the ground of protection.

findings.text: 6.5 ◆ Fringe (M26): "my beloved with whom my soul is well pleased. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will proclaim justice" (Mat 12:18) [D1] — God's soul, God's Spirit and justice in one sentence; "the souls of those who had been beheaded … authority to judge was committed" (Rev 20:4); "God appointed a scorching east wind … he asked that he might die" (Jon 4:8) → Batch G §6

7. Cross-cutting observations for Batch H [Claude reading]: The most powerful heart is shown as the least its own. The king's heart is turned, filled, stirred, hardened and cut off by God (§1.1). When it claims a throne for itself, it falls (§1.2). Deu 17:20's daily reading is the one preventive.; Allegiance is a heart-matter, and it moves by attention and kinship. Absalom steals hearts by hearing their causes. David sways them back by "bone and flesh". Abimelech uses the same flesh-claim to incline hearts toward fratricide (§1.3).; The social relations of this batch supply the vocabulary for the self's relation to itself: rule: one rules one's spirit; peace rules the heart (§1.5); service: one serves from the heart, or serves sin with the flesh (§3.1); guarding: one keeps one's heart, soul and spirit (§5.1); judgment: the heart condemns or justifies the self (§6.2); Setting-words turned inward describe the inner seat as governed. This is the batch's main contribution.; More words with opposite value by circumstance (for synthesis item 3): *nāṣar*: keep the heart (Pro 4:23) / the "guarded" wily heart (Pro 7:10) (§5.1); *šāmar*: keep the law / God keeps the soul / enemies watch for the life (§5.2); vengeance: malice in the soul / redemption in God's heart / comfort to the anxious heart (§6.1); fatness: a satisfied soul / a dull heart (§2.3); *šāgâ*: unwitting error / self-accusation / intoxication (§4.2); the heart "lifted up": courage in the Lord's ways / pride (2Ch 17:6; already in Batch D); kinship-flesh: restoration (David) / fratricide (Abimelech) (§1.3); A life has a price in law and in narrative, but not before God (§2.2; §1.4). This qualifies Batch G §5.4.; The eating-and-drinking threshold, extended (Batch F §7): Esther's wine-banquets: Haman leaves "joyful and glad of heart" → wrath → gallows (Est 5:6–14). At the second banquet the king rises "from the wine-drinking" in wrath, and Haman begs for his life (7:7–8). The same banquet is the threshold for Esther's petition and for Haman's fall.; The threshold refused at the heart: "Daniel resolved [*set on his heart*] that he would not defile himself with the king's food, or with the wine" (Dan 1:8) → "fatter in flesh" than those who ate it (1:15). Compare Uriah (Batch F §7.5).; The inner sentence before the feast: "My master is delayed" → eat, drink, get drunk → the master arrives (Luk 12:45–46; §3.2).

findings.text: 7. Cross-cutting observations for Batch H [Claude reading]: The warning: "watch yourselves lest your hearts be weighed down with dissipation and drunkenness" (Luk 21:34).; The counter-statement: "the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking but of … joy in the Holy Spirit" (Rom 14:17).; David's heart reads kings rightly. Both flights to Achish begin in the heart (1Sa 21:12; 27:1). The second follows immediately on Saul's oath and confession (26:21–25) (§1.8).; Voices addressed to the soul — beyond self-address (for synthesis item 1): Others speak to my soul: "Flee like a bird" (Psa 11:1); God swears by his own soul (Amo 6:8; Jer 51:14); God's soul is burdened (Isa 1:14) and avenges itself (Jer 5:9); Fringe worth keeping: the king's heart read by Joab (2Sa 14:1); bitterness of soul as the recruiting ground of a king (1Sa 22:2); the queen of Sheba's mind filled and spirit emptied (1Ki 10:2, 5); Haman's riches "worth nothing" to a heart fixed on Mordecai (Est 5:13); the soul's "burden" as its desire (Eze 24:25); Moses' despair answered by distributing the Spirit (Num 11); the watchman who delivers his own soul (Eze 33:9); Eli killed by the word "ark" (1Sa 4:18); Mary keeping what she did not understand (Luk 2:50–51); the sons of Sceva mastered by the spirit (Act 19:16); Simon's money exposing his heart (Act 8:21); the good intention set aside overnight (2Sa 7:3–5); "he who seeks my life seeks your life" (1Sa 22:23); Balaam's soul wishing for the death of the upright (Num 23:10)
